newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes at lowest since December 1985.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes at lowest since December 1985.

text.p: Gold trading was choppy and nervous on Friday afternoon after the market fell to near 12 year lows overnight, dealers said.
The New York markets were closed for the U.S. Independence Day holiday, thinning market volume.
Bullion fixed at $324.45 per ounce down from $325.20 on Friday morning and making the fix the lowest since late December 1985.
"Nobody in the world can be bullish for gold just now," a dealer said forecasting a serious test of the psychologically critical $300.00 price within a week or two.
An already weak market lost all heart after a statement from the Reserve Bank of Australia confirmed it had sold 167 tonnes of bullion from its gold reserves over the past six months.
After being steady initially in Europe, the price plunged around $10.00 when the U.S. investment funds took the Australian central bank news as a signal to sell the market.
The pattern was repeated in Asia where physical buying was swamped by investor long liquidation.
London and Europe adjusted into line this morning but the price drift continued southwards as books were squared and the prospect of even lower prices was faced.
"The Australians sold over six months so that is around a tonne of gold per day. The market wouldn't even blink at that but the point is it puts pressure on the other central banks," a dealer said
Further gold sales by central banks cannot be ruled out after the latest confirmation of recent sales by Australia's central bank, Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said in a market report on Friday.
The bank said it would favour official gold sales in the form of coin issues and auctions rather than sudden news of past sales which caused chaos in the market.
Before the $300.00 came on to the chart interim support at $315/$316 will be tested.
After $300.00 the targets become lows hit in March 1985 at between $287.25 and $284.25, dealers said.
The other precious metals slipped into gold's shadows.
Silver lost value overnight and failed to regain losses after fixing at its lowest level since March 1995.
It was indicated at $4.56/$4.58 down eight cents.
Platinum was quiet at $419.00/$423.00 down $4.00 and palladium edged either side of its $189.50/$194.50 close.
